---
title: "Are we sure the model is correctly using the NACA 0006 airfoil?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

The section is checked three ways — that the geometry is what it claims, that
every surface carries it, and that NeuralFoil returns a symmetric polar from it
— and then the choice itself is tested by giving each surface the section its
own chords imply.

::: {.callout-note}
## Assumed
Matching a surface to its own t/c means picking a NACA section of that
thickness. That is the nearest available stand-in, not the same thing as a
square-cut plate — which is the point the answer turns on.
:::

```{python}
af = asb.Airfoil("naca0006")
print(f"max thickness {af.max_thickness():.4f}, max camber {af.max_camber():.6f}")
for w in mceagle.wings:
    print(f"{w.name:11s} sections carry {set(x.airfoil.name for x in w.xsecs)}")

a2 = np.linspace(-4, 4, 9)
for Re in [1.6e3, 3.6e4]:                 # the fin tip, and the mean chord
    r = af.get_aero_from_neuralfoil(alpha=a2, Re=Re)
    print(f"Re {Re:7.0f}: CL(0) {np.array(r['CL'])[4]:+.2e}, "
          f"dCL/dalpha {np.polyfit(a2, np.array(r['CL']), 1)[0]:.4f} /deg "
          f"(thin-airfoil 0.1097), confidence "
          f"{float(np.array(r['analysis_confidence'])[0]):.2f}")
```

```{python}
tc = {}
for nm, etas, chords in [("wing", wing_eta, wing_c), ("stab", stab_eta, stab_c),
                         ("fin", fin_eta, fin_c)]:
    t = t_foam / chords * 100
    tc[nm] = np.trapezoid(t * chords, etas) / np.trapezoid(chords, etas)

# Lift-curve slope against thickness, at the fin's own Reynolds number.
slope = {}
for nm in ["naca0006", "naca0008", "naca0010", "naca0013"]:
    r = asb.Airfoil(nm).get_aero_from_neuralfoil(alpha=a2, Re=1.56e4)
    slope[nm] = np.polyfit(a2, np.array(r["CL"]), 1)[0]
```

```{python}
def swap(af_w, af_h, af_v):
    """The airframe rebuilt with a chosen section on each surface."""
    xs = lambda le, eta, c, af, **kw: asb.WingXSec(xyz_le=le, chord=c,
                                                   airfoil=af, **kw)
    return asb.Airplane(
        name="v", fuselages=mceagle.fuselages, s_ref=S_w, c_ref=c_w, b_ref=b_w,
        xyz_ref=[x_qc_w, 0, 0],
        wings=[
            asb.Wing(name="Wing", symmetric=True, xsecs=[
                xs([x_le_w, e*b_w/2, e*z_tip], e, c, af_w)
                for e, c in zip(wing_eta, wing_c)]),
            asb.Wing(name="Stabilizer", symmetric=True, xsecs=[
                xs([x_le_h, e*b_h/2, z_h], e, c, af_h, twist=i_h)
                for e, c in zip(stab_eta, stab_c)]),
            asb.Wing(name="Fin", xsecs=[
                xs([x_te_v - c, 0, e*b_v], e, c, af_v)
                for e, c in zip(fin_eta, fin_c)]),
        ])


mp0 = mass_properties()


def Cn_beta(ap, alpha=4.0, V=6.0):
    """Directional stability, about the airplane's own moment reference."""
    d = asb.AeroBuildup(
        airplane=ap, op_point=asb.OperatingPoint(velocity=V, alpha=alpha)
    ).run_with_stability_derivatives(alpha=False, p=False, q=False, r=False)
    return float(np.array(d["Cnb"]).ravel()[0])


matched = swap(*map(asb.Airfoil, ["naca0006", "naca0008", "naca0013"]))
arms = {}
for label, ap in [("all 0006, as modelled", mceagle),
                  ("stab 0008, fin 0013", matched)]:
    x_np = neutral_point(ap)
    arms[label] = (x_np, ballast_for(x_np - 0.10 * c_w, 0.0, mp0), Cn_beta(ap))

# Cn_beta above is about the model's moment reference at the wing quarter-chord.
# The aircraft does not pivot there -- it pivots about its CG, which ballasting
# puts further aft, shortening the fin's arm. Same airframe, moved reference.
x_cg_10 = arms["all 0006, as modelled"][0] - 0.10 * c_w
about_cg = asb.Airplane(
    name="v", wings=mceagle.wings, fuselages=mceagle.fuselages,
    s_ref=S_w, c_ref=c_w, b_ref=b_w, xyz_ref=[x_cg_10, 0, 0],
)
Cnb_about_cg = Cn_beta(about_cg)
```

**Answer.** Yes, mechanically. The geometry is a true NACA 0006 —
`{python} f"{af.max_thickness()*100:.2f}"`% thick, zero camber — every section
of all three surfaces carries it, and NeuralFoil returns CL(0) = 0 to machine
precision with a slope near thin-airfoil theory, still at high confidence down
at the fin tip's Re of 1,600.

What is not right is the reason recorded for choosing it. Six percent matches
the wing's mean chord and nothing else: the same 5 mm foam is
`{python} f"{tc['stab']:.1f}"`% of the stabilizer's chord and
`{python} f"{tc['fin']:.1f}"`% of the fin's (@tbl-tc). Matching those makes the model
worse. NeuralFoil's smooth sections shed lift-curve slope quickly at this scale
(@tbl-thickness) — so a 13% fin flips Cn_beta from
`{python} f"{arms['all 0006, as modelled'][2]:+.4f}"` to
`{python} f"{arms['stab 0008, fin 0013'][2]:+.4f}"` and the aircraft loses
directional stability. A square-cut plate does not behave that way, because its
sharp edge fixes separation and reattachment. One thin section on every surface
is therefore the right model of a flat plate, and being thinner than the tail's
true t/c is the point rather than an error.

One consequence for later work: the Cn_beta above is taken about the model's
moment reference at the wing quarter-chord, `{python} f"{x_qc_w*1e3:.1f}"` mm.
About the ballasted CG at `{python} f"{x_cg_10*1e3:.1f}"` mm it is
`{python} f"{Cnb_about_cg:+.4f}"` /rad —
`{python} f"{Cnb_about_cg/arms['all 0006, as modelled'][2]*100:.0f}"`% of the
figure quoted above, because the fin's arm is shorter from there.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-tc
#| tbl-cap: "What 5 mm of foam is worth as a thickness ratio on each surface, against the 6% every surface is modelled at."
import pandas as pd

pd.DataFrame({
    "surface": list(tc),
    "area-weighted t/c [%]": [f"{v:.1f}" for v in tc.values()],
    "modelled as [%]": ["6.0"] * len(tc),
}).style.hide(axis="index")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-thickness
#| tbl-cap: "What NeuralFoil's lift-curve slope does as a symmetric section is thickened, at the fin's own Reynolds number of 15,600."
pd.DataFrame({
    "section": list(slope),
    "dCL/dα [/deg]": [f"{v:+.4f}" for v in slope.values()],
}).style.hide(axis="index")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-matched
#| tbl-cap: "The airframe as modelled, against the same airframe with each surface given the section its own chords imply."
pd.DataFrame({
    "airframe": list(arms),
    "neutral point [mm]": [f"{v[0]*1e3:.1f}" for v in arms.values()],
    "ballast for 10% MAC [g]": [f"{v[1]*1e3:.2f}" for v in arms.values()],
    "Cn_beta [/rad]": [f"{v[2]:+.4f}" for v in arms.values()],
}).style.hide(axis="index")
```
